## QG-ALL-SML-0009 — Local variables should be used

A local variable is declared and assigned but its value is never read.

### Why is this a problem?

The computation behind the value is paid for and thrown away. More importantly, an unread variable is
often the tail of a change that was left half-done: the new value was computed but the code that was
supposed to use it still reads the old one.

### How to fix it

Use the value where it was meant to be used, or remove the declaration and the expression that fed
it. If a name is needed only to document a discarded result, prefix it with an underscore.

## QG-CSS-SML-0005 — Declarations should not rely on the important flag

A declaration is marked as important.

### Why is this a problem?

The flag wins over specificity, so the next developer who needs a different value has to add another
important flag, and the stylesheet gradually loses the cascade as a working mechanism. Overrides then
depend on file order, which is exactly what CSS was designed to avoid.

### How to fix it

Increase the specificity of the selector or reorganise the rules so the intended declaration wins
naturally. Keep the flag for third-party styles you cannot change.

## QG-RS-BUG-0007 — Fallible results should not be unwrapped

A Result or Option is unwrapped without handling the failure case.

### Why is this a problem?

Unwrap turns a value the type system asked you to handle into an abort. In a service that means the
task or the process dies on input that was merely unexpected, and the message points at the unwrap
rather than at the cause.

### How to fix it

Propagate with the question-mark operator, or handle the case with match, unwrap_or or ok_or. Keep
expect for invariants that genuinely cannot be violated, and let its message explain why.

#### Wrong

```rs
let config = std::fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap();
```

#### Fixed

```rs
let config = std::fs::read_to_string(path)?;
```

## QG-CS-SEC-0010 — Insecure cookie configuration

A cookie is written without the flags that keep it out of scripts and off plain HTTP.

### Why is this a problem?

Without HttpOnly, any injected script can read the cookie and send the session elsewhere; without
Secure, the browser also sends it over plain HTTP where it can be captured on the network. Both flags
cost one line each and are the difference between a session that survives a small XSS and one that is
handed to the attacker.

### How to fix it

Set HttpOnly and Secure on the CookieOptions, and add SameSite to limit cross-site sending. For
authentication cookies, configure it once in the cookie options of the auth handler.

#### Wrong

```cs
Response.Cookies.Append("session", token);
```

#### Fixed

```cs
Response.Cookies.Append("session", token, new CookieOptions
{
    HttpOnly = true, Secure = true, SameSite = SameSiteMode.Strict
});
```

fullDescription.text: A method is declared async void outside of an event handler.

help.text:
Return Task, or Task<T> when there is a result, and await the call. Keep async void only for event
handlers, and wrap their body in a try/catch so nothing escapes.
help.markdown:
## QG-CS-BUG-0001 — Async void methods

A method is declared async void outside of an event handler.

### Why is this a problem?

The caller gets no task, so it cannot wait for the work or observe its result. An exception thrown
after the first await is raised on the synchronization context instead of at the call site, which
usually means an unhandled exception that takes down the process.

### How to fix it

Return Task, or Task<T> when there is a result, and await the call. Keep async void only for event
handlers, and wrap their body in a try/catch so nothing escapes.

#### Wrong

```cs
public async void SaveAsync() { await repository.SaveAsync(); }
```

#### Fixed

```cs
public async Task SaveAsync() { await repository.SaveAsync(); }
```

properties.remediationEffort: Return Task from async methods instead of void.

fullDescription.text: A file is opened using a path that includes values coming from outside the program.

help.text:
Keep the caller from choosing the path: map an identifier to a file name yourself, or resolve the
combined path and verify it still starts with the folder you intended before opening it.
help.markdown:
## QG-CS-SEC-0018 — Path traversal via file operations

A file is opened using a path that includes values coming from outside the program.

### Why is this a problem?

Path segments such as ../ are resolved by the file system, not by the application, so an input that
looks like a file name can reach configuration files or keys elsewhere on the disk. Path.Combine does
not prevent this and will happily discard your base folder if the input is rooted.

### How to fix it

Keep the caller from choosing the path: map an identifier to a file name yourself, or resolve the
combined path and verify it still starts with the folder you intended before opening it.

#### Wrong

```cs
var path = Path.Combine(root, Request.Query["file"]);
return File.ReadAllBytes(path);
```

#### Fixed

```cs
var full = Path.GetFullPath(Path.Combine(root, name));
if (!full.StartsWith(root, StringComparison.Ordinal)) return Forbid();
return File.ReadAllBytes(full);
```

properties.remediationEffort: Validate the path and restrict it to an allow listed directory.

rules.name: Count() used to test for emptiness

shortDescription.text: Count() used to test for emptiness

fullDescription.text: A Count() result is compared with zero to decide whether a sequence has elements.

help.text:
Replace the comparison with Any(), or with !Any() for the empty case. Keep Count() only when the
number itself is used.
help.markdown:
## QG-CS-SML-0018 — Count() used to test for emptiness

A Count() result is compared with zero to decide whether a sequence has elements.

### Why is this a problem?

Count() walks the entire sequence, and on a database query it becomes an aggregate over the whole
table. Any() stops at the first element, and translates to EXISTS, which is what the question
actually asks.

### How to fix it

Replace the comparison with Any(), or with !Any() for the empty case. Keep Count() only when the
number itself is used.

#### Wrong

```cs
if (orders.Count() > 0) { ... }
```

#### Fixed

```cs
if (orders.Any()) { ... }
```

properties.remediationEffort: Use Any() instead of Count() when testing for emptiness.

rules.name: Antiforgery validation should not be switched off

shortDescription.text: Antiforgery validation should not be switched off

fullDescription.text: An MVC controller or action opts out of antiforgery token validation.

help.text:
Remove the opt-out and let the framework validate the token. If the endpoint is a machine-to-machine
API, authenticate it with a bearer token or an API key instead of cookies, which removes the need for
antiforgery in the first place.
help.markdown:
## QG-CS-SEC-0032 — Antiforgery validation should not be switched off

An MVC controller or action opts out of antiforgery token validation.

### Why is this a problem?

Antiforgery tokens are what stop another site from making a logged-in browser submit a request to
yours. Once validation is disabled, any page on the internet can trigger the action with the user's
cookies attached, and the request looks completely legitimate on the server side.

### How to fix it

Remove the opt-out and let the framework validate the token. If the endpoint is a machine-to-machine
API, authenticate it with a bearer token or an API key instead of cookies, which removes the need for
antiforgery in the first place.

#### Wrong

```cs
[HttpPost]
[IgnoreAntiforgeryToken]
public IActionResult Transfer(TransferModel model) { ... }
```

#### Fixed

```cs
[HttpPost]
[ValidateAntiForgeryToken]
public IActionResult Transfer(TransferModel model) { ... }
```

shortDescription.text: Entity Framework raw SQL should not be assembled from values

fullDescription.text: A raw SQL call receives a query that is concatenated or interpolated at run time.

help.text:
Pass values as parameters: use the FromSql/ExecuteSql overloads that take a FormattableString, or
supply explicit DbParameter objects. Never concatenate the value into the command text.
help.markdown:
## QG-CS-SEC-0038 — Entity Framework raw SQL should not be assembled from values

A raw SQL call receives a query that is concatenated or interpolated at run time.

### Why is this a problem?

The raw SQL escape hatch sends the string to the database exactly as built. A value that contains a
quote changes the shape of the statement, which is all an attacker needs to read other tables or drop
the filter that limits the rows they see.

### How to fix it

Pass values as parameters: use the FromSql/ExecuteSql overloads that take a FormattableString, or
supply explicit DbParameter objects. Never concatenate the value into the command text.

#### Wrong

```cs
context.Users.FromSqlRaw("SELECT * FROM Users WHERE Name = '" + name + "'");
```

#### Fixed

```cs
context.Users.FromSql($"SELECT * FROM Users WHERE Name = {name}");
```

shortDescription.text: Secrets should not be written to logs

fullDescription.text: A logging call mentions a password, token or key value.

help.text:
Log an identifier instead of the value, or redact it explicitly. Where a payload must be logged for
diagnosis, strip the sensitive fields before it reaches the logger.
help.markdown:
## QG-CS-SEC-0044 — Secrets should not be written to logs

A logging call mentions a password, token or key value.

### Why is this a problem?

Logs travel much further than the code that writes them: they are shipped to aggregators, kept for
months and read by people who never had access to production data. A secret written once stays
recoverable long after it has been rotated — assuming anyone notices it was exposed at all.

### How to fix it

Log an identifier instead of the value, or redact it explicitly. Where a payload must be logged for
diagnosis, strip the sensitive fields before it reaches the logger.

shortDescription.text: Regular expressions on user input should have a timeout

fullDescription.text: A regex is evaluated against request data with no matching timeout configured.

help.text:
Pass a matching timeout when constructing the Regex or calling the static methods, and simplify the
pattern to avoid nested quantifiers on the same input.
help.markdown:
## QG-CS-SEC-0045 — Regular expressions on user input should have a timeout

A regex is evaluated against request data with no matching timeout configured.

### Why is this a problem?

Backtracking makes some patterns take exponential time on inputs designed to trigger it, so a single
short request can pin a CPU core for minutes. Without a timeout there is nothing to interrupt it, and
a handful of requests take the service down.

### How to fix it

Pass a matching timeout when constructing the Regex or calling the static methods, and simplify the
pattern to avoid nested quantifiers on the same input.

#### Wrong

```cs
if (Regex.IsMatch(userInput, pattern)) { ... }
```

#### Fixed

```cs
if (Regex.IsMatch(userInput, pattern, RegexOptions.None, TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(200))) { ... }
```

shortDescription.text: HttpClient instances should not be created per request

fullDescription.text: A new HttpClient is constructed instead of being obtained from the factory.

help.text:
Register the client with AddHttpClient and inject IHttpClientFactory or a typed client. The factory
keeps handlers pooled and rotates them so DNS changes are honoured.
help.markdown:
## QG-CS-PRF-0002 — HttpClient instances should not be created per request

A new HttpClient is constructed instead of being obtained from the factory.

### Why is this a problem?

Each instance holds its own connection pool, and disposing it leaves sockets in TIME_WAIT for
minutes. Under load the process runs out of ports and every outgoing call starts failing, while a
long-lived single instance never picks up DNS changes.

### How to fix it

Register the client with AddHttpClient and inject IHttpClientFactory or a typed client. The factory
keeps handlers pooled and rotates them so DNS changes are honoured.

#### Wrong

```cs
using var client = new HttpClient();
```

#### Fixed

```cs
public OrdersClient(HttpClient client) { _client = client; }  // registered via AddHttpClient
```

## QG-CS-SEC-0037 — Raw HTML should not be produced from values that are not constants

A non-constant value is passed to a helper that emits unescaped HTML.

### Why is this a problem?

Razor encodes output by default; these helpers exist to bypass that. Whatever reaches them is
inserted into the page as markup, so a value containing a script tag becomes executable code running
with the user's session.

### How to fix it

Render the value normally so the framework encodes it. When the goal is formatting, build the markup
from a fixed template and interpolate only encoded values, or sanitize with a dedicated HTML
sanitizer before rendering.

```cs
@Html.Raw(model.Comment)
```

#### Fixed

```cs
@model.Comment
```

## QG-RAZ-SEC-0001 — Views should not disable the antiforgery token on forms

A Razor form explicitly turns the antiforgery token off.

### Why is this a problem?

The token is what ties the submitted form to the user's session. Without it, a form hosted on another
domain can post to this action with the user's cookies, and the server has no way to tell the two
apart.

### How to fix it

helper when the form is written by hand.

help.text:

help.markdown:
## QG-RAZ-SEC-0002 — Views should not build markup from model values

A view renders a value through a helper that bypasses HTML encoding.

### Why is this a problem?

Razor encodes every expression by default, which is why views are normally safe. These helpers exist
to opt out of that, and once a model value flows through them any markup it contains becomes part of
the page and runs in the visitor's browser.

### How to fix it

Print the value directly so it is encoded. If it must contain markup, sanitize it server-side with a
library that keeps a strict allow-list of tags and attributes.

## QG-RAZ-SEC-0003 — Views should not contain inline scripts driven by model data

Model data is written into a JavaScript block in the view.

### Why is this a problem?

Inside a script block the HTML encoder is the wrong encoder: a value containing a quote or a closing
script tag ends the string or the block and the rest is executed as code. Inline scripts also force a
permissive content security policy, which removes a second line of defence.

### How to fix it

it from an external script file. That keeps the page compatible with a strict content security policy.

## QG-CS-SEC-0046 — Legacy VB compiler options should stay enabled

A VB.NET file disables Option Strict or Option Explicit.

### Why is this a problem?

With these options off the compiler accepts undeclared variables and silent narrowing conversions, so
a typo becomes a new variable and a type mismatch becomes a run-time failure in production instead of
an error at build time.

### How to fix it

reports. Convert them explicitly where the narrowing is intended.
